title: Copilot Cowork: access Business Applications through Work IQ and use business skills
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documents the administrator-installed preview plugin, Cowork consumption billing, and the listed controls and API operations. The two cited App Access guides give different navigation instructions; the control note should flag that difference.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Cowork access to Business Applications through Work IQ and business skills for enterprise-data-grounded processes.
claims.quote: Users can access Business Applications through Work IQ in Copilot Cowork and use Business Skills to complete end-to-end business processes grounded in their enterprise data and apps.

claims.quote: Access through Cowork is available in public preview.

claims.quote: An admin must install the Business apps (preview) plugin for users. Users can't add the plugin in Cowork until an admin installs it for them.

claims.quote: Create a follow-up task for the account owner

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork examples include reassigning account ownership.
claims.quote: Reassign account ownership

claims.claim: Microsoft's Cowork examples include escalating an unresolved case.

claims.claim: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.
claims.quote: Power Apps model-driven apps are available as Business Applications in Work IQ.

claims.claim: Work IQ uses an app's views, forms and tables to complete requests.
claims.quote: Work IQ uses the app's views, forms, and tables to complete the request.

claims.claim: Business skills are business-process instructions stored in a Dataverse environment.
claims.quote: The business skill is saved in the environment you used to connect to the Dataverse MCP server or a relevant environment through Work IQ.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: After activation, Copilot Chat, Cowork and connected agents can discover and use business skills they have access to.
claims.quote: After you create and activate business skills in your environment, Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork, and connected agents can discover and use the skills you have access to and follow your organization's processes.

claims.claim: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ MCP is generally available.
claims.quote: Access to Business Applications through Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Microsoft Copilot Studio is generally available.

claims.claim: The plugin install path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Plugins > Business apps (preview) > Install.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools > Plugins. ... In the Name column, select Business apps (preview). ... In the Business apps (preview) panel, select the Install button.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented automation to install this Business apps plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business apps" "Cowork" plugin install API automation. Opened Cowork plugin setup, Manage plugins for Copilot Cowork, and Package Management API overview/block; none gives installation automation for this plugin.

claims.claim: Plugin installation can target All users or Specific users and groups.
claims.quote: In the Installed for field, select All users or Specific users and groups.

claims.claim: The tenant audience path is Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Settings > View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.
claims.quote: In the left navigation pane, select Copilot > Settings. ... In Copilot settings, select View all > Business Applications data in Work IQ available to Copilot.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has not documented an API for the tenant Business Applications audience setting.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business Applications" "Work IQ" tenant audience setting API PowerShell; "Business Applications data in Work IQ" PowerShell API. Opened default-settings, manage-ai-experience-access and quickstart; no API for this setting found.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The audience choices are All users, Specific groups and No users, with All users the default.
claims.quote: To turn off access for everyone, select No users. ... To turn on access for everyone, select All users. This option is the default. ... To provide access to a limited audience, select Specific groups

claims.claim: The quickstart uses a slightly different label for the tenant audience setting.
claims.quote: Open the setting for Business Applications in Work IQ available to Copilot in Microsoft 365 Copilot.

claims.claim: Learn names AI Administrator for Microsoft 365 admin center experience-access settings.
claims.quote: AI Administrator role to work with settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Environment Work IQ is configured in Power Platform admin center > Manage > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Work IQ.
claims.quote: Select Manage, and select the environment. ... Select Settings > Product > Features. ... Locate Work IQ. ... Turn on Work IQ if it's currently off.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn has not documented an API for the environment Work IQ participation switch.
claims.quote: Searched: "Work IQ" environment enable setting API organization PowerShell; "Dataverse intelligence" "API" "setting" enable. Opened manage-participation, default-settings and Business Applications overview; no API for this switch found.

claims.claim: Learn names Power Platform Administrator for environment participation and application-access administration.
claims.quote: Power Platform Administrator role to manage settings and assign other roles.

claims.where: controls[2].note; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Work IQ participation settings do not prevent agentic access to environment data.
claims.quote: These participation settings don't prevent agentic access to environment data. Use App Access controls to manage that access.

claims.claim: The feature's App Access guide gives Power Platform admin center > Security > Identity & access > App Access Control > environment > Enable.
claims.quote: Select Security > Identity & access. ... Select App Access Control. ... Select the environment in which you want to enable app access. ... Select Enable, and then select Save.
claims.fix: Append to controls[3].note and its rendered note: 'The general App Access guide gives a different route after selecting the environment: Set up app access control > Access control > Enabled, then select an application and Block.' The other cited guide is https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/control-app-access-environment#turn-on-enabled-mode.

claims.claim: PATCH https://<organization>/api/data/v9.2/applications(<applicationid>) updates a Dataverse application entry.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /applications(applicationid) ... See Update

claims.claim: The applications request body uses access, with 0 for Allowed and 1 for Blocked.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/applications ... access ... Application Access ... 0 | Allowed ... 1 | Blocked

claims.claim: Changing an app's Allowed or Blocked entry is distinct from enabling environment-level App Access enforcement.
claims.quote: If you set some apps to Allowed or Blocked, you don't need to remove the setting when the app access control feature is turned off to Disabled. There are no app restrictions in this environment.

claims.claim: The general App Access guide requires a managed environment.
claims.quote: Verify that your environment is a managed environment ... Your environment must be a managed environment.

claims.claim: App Access controls which applications, including Cowork, can access an environment's data.
claims.quote: App Access is the mechanism used to choose which applications, including agentic applications such as Copilot Cowork, are allowed to access data in a particular environment.

claims.claim: Spending limits are under Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > policy > Spending limits.
claims.quote: go to Copilot > Cost Management. ... Select the Configuration tab. ... Select the spending policy you want to edit. ... The spending policy details fly-out opens ... Spending limits

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} updates a spending policy.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id} ... PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/3f9e2c1a-0000-0000-0000-00000000c21b

claims.claim: The spending policy PATCH request supports periodLimit and perUserLimit.
claims.quote: The following properties can be updated: displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit, and billingMethods.

claims.where: controls[4].note; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Spending policies govern selected services and users and provide policy-level and per-user limits.
claims.quote: Spending policies let you choose the users and services covered, set a shared monthly limit, add a per-user limit, and receive alerts as consumption approaches a threshold.

claims.claim: The spending policy API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: A skill is deactivated in Power Apps > environment > More > Business skills > skill > Deactivate.
claims.quote: Go to Power Apps and select your environment. ... select More, and then select Business skills. ... Select a skill, and then select Deactivate from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.claim: PATCH /skills(<skillid>) can change a skill's state using statecode and statuscode.
claims.quote: SetState ... PATCH /skills(skillid) ... Update the statecode and statuscode properties.

claims.claim: A skill statecode value of 1 means Inactive.
claims.quote: statecode Choices/Options ... 1 | Label: Inactive DefaultStatus: 2 InvariantName: Inactive

claims.claim: A skill statuscode value of 2 means Inactive and corresponds to statecode 1.
claims.quote: statuscode Choices/Options ... 2 | Label: Inactive State:1 TransitionData: None

claims.claim: Deactivation stops skill discovery and use without deleting the skill.
claims.quote: To stop agents from discovering or using an active skill: ... select Deactivate ... Deactivating a skill preserves its content and version history.

claims.claim: Share on the Business skills page configures skill sharing.
claims.quote: Select a skill, and then select Share from the command bar or the three-dot menu

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope: Default environments
claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments, subject to exceptions.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ is on by default for new public production environments created for new or existing tenants. The following environments are exceptions:

claims.claim: EU and EFTA environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: European Union (EU) and European Free Trade Association (EFTA) environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned in the EU and EFTA macro region geography.

claims.claim: Government-related environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Government-related environments: This exception applies to environments provisioned by customers with current or previous government cloud deployments that are likely to depend on FedRAMP security controls.

claims.claim: Trial, sandbox and developer environments are exceptions to default enablement.
claims.quote: Nonproduction environments: This exception applies to trial, sandbox, and developer environments.

claims.claim: The existing-environment enablement plan has been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.
claims.quote: The plan to turn on Business Applications in Work IQ for existing environments that aren't listed as exceptionshas been deferred from the previously documented November 2026 schedule.

claims.claim: Business Applications in Work IQ is not currently available in sovereign or government clouds, including DoD, GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: Business Applications in Work IQ isn't currently available in sovereign or government cloud environments, including Department of Defense (DoD), Government Community Cloud (GCC), and GCC High.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ respects existing user permissions and does not grant additional business-data access.
claims.quote: Work IQ respects your existing Power Platform security permissions. ... Work IQ doesn't grant additional access to business data.

claims.claim: For US tenants using FedRAMP-accredited environments, enabling Work IQ might send data outside the FedRAMP authorization boundary.
claims.quote: This information applies to tenants provisioned in the United States that use FedRAMP-accredited environments ... Enabling Work IQ might cause data to flow from the tenant's FedRAMP-accredited environment to Microsoft 365, which is outside the applicable FedRAMP authorization boundary.

claims.claim: The plugin connection procedure includes credential selection and entering a sign-in number in Authenticator.
claims.quote: Select your credentials. A number appears to approve your sign in request. ... Enter the number in the Authenticator app.

claims.claim: Business skills are user-owned by default.
claims.quote: Skills are user-owned by default.

claims.claim: Business skills can be shared with everyone in the environment.
claims.quote: General access—Makes the skill available to everyone in the environment.

claims.claim: Security-role-based skill access requires both the shared-with security role and Skill Sharing Role.
claims.quote: An administrator must assign users the Skill Sharing Role, either directly or through a team. Users must also have the security role that the skill is shared with.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Work IQ supports creating and updating business records.
claims.quote: Read, create, and update records by using the default main form, or name another main form in your prompt.

claims.claim: Users review proposed values and explicitly confirm data changes before submission.
claims.quote: For an operation that changes data, review the proposed values, make any needed changes, and explicitly confirm the operation before it's submitted.

claims.claim: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.
claims.quote: Delete operations also require explicit confirmation.

claims.claim: Skills can be created or updated through Copilot or a connected agent.
claims.quote: You can also create and update skills through Copilot or an agent connected to Work IQ or the Dataverse MCP server

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends testing each skill with a repeatable scenario before broad sharing.
claims.quote: Test each skill with a repeatable scenario before you share it broadly.

claims.claim: Work IQ cannot create or update records when the selected form has OnLoad, OnChange or OnSave JavaScript handlers.
claims.quote: You can't create or update a record when the selected form has JavaScript OnLoad, OnChange, or OnSave event handlers.

claims.claim: Custom controls and subgrids are not supported.
claims.quote: Custom controls and subgrids aren't supported.

claims.claim: The Business skills page does not currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback.
claims.quote: The Business skills page doesn't currently show per-skill runtime usage or feedback. Use controlled test cases and any logs or traces provided by the agent experience to collect evidence.

claims.where: summary; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Work IQ consumption supporting a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork consumption.
claims.quote: Business context accessed through Cowork contributes to Cowork consumption. ... Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Copilot Credits are the unit for the participating usage-based experiences.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences.

claims.claim: Prepaid capacity packs can fund this consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription can fund this consumption.
claims.quote: Prepaid capacity packs and pay-as-you-go billing through an Azure subscription provide ways to fund that consumption.

claims.claim: Separately reported Work IQ API consumption is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.
claims.quote: Direct calls through the Work IQ API are reported under Work IQ API. ... Work IQ API consumption can include both Microsoft 365 productivity context and business applications context. Its total is not a Business Applications-only cost breakdown.

claims.where: Why it matters; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps, so task consumption varies rather than being a fixed-price prompt.
claims.quote: One user request can involve multiple tool calls and reasoning steps. Work IQ includes deterministic operations and variable-cost contextual reasoning, so a prompt isn't necessarily a single fixed-price operation.

claims.where: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature pages publish no per-task Copilot Credit rate for Cowork business-context requests.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cowork" "business context" "rate" credits; "Cowork" "Business apps" plugin license licensing per task rate Copilot Credits. Opened understand-costs, plugin setup and Plan licensing and cost; results explain variable consumption, not a fixed feature-specific per-task rate.

claims.claim: Learn names no separate feature-specific licence for the Business apps plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: "Cowork" "Business apps" plugin license licensing per task rate Copilot Credits. Opened plugin setup, understand-costs, Plan licensing and cost, Work IQ API licensing and Manage plugins. General Cowork licensing is documented; no separate Business apps plugin SKU was found.

claims.claim: Cowork experiences can vary with an organization's apps, licences, policies and available services.
claims.quote: Some experiences might vary based on your organization's apps, licenses, policies, and available services.

claims.claim: A spending policy covering Cowork can cap Cowork credit consumption using policy and per-user limits.
claims.quote: When users hit the limit, they lose access to agents and services for the rest of the month until credits reset on the first of the month. ... Specify the maximum credit limit users can spend per month.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Preview services can change and underlying application services can continue to incur licence fees during a consumption-based preview.
claims.quote: Preview offerings are provided as-is and may be modified or discontinued at any time. For consumption-based services, usage of underlying application services may continue to incur license fees during the preview period.

claims.claim: Users need permission to the Power Platform environment, model-driven app and business data involved.
claims.quote: You need permission to access the Power Platform environment, model-driven app, and business data involved in your request.

claims.claim: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment.
claims.quote: A Power Platform administrator must enable Work IQ for the environment in the Power Platform admin center.

claims.claim: Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps must be Default or On for the app.
claims.quote: For the model-driven app, the Enable M365 Copilot in model-driven apps setting (m365copilotmodelappenabled) must be set to Default or On.

claims.claim: Enabling an experience does not itself grant business-data access.
claims.quote: Enabling an experience doesn't grant access to business data.

claims.claim: The Package Management API has an operation that blocks a Copilot package to prevent its usage.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage.

claims.claim: The package block API is beta.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version are subject to change. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 licence.
claims.quote: Access to the Package Management API requires a Microsoft Agent 365 license.

claims.claim: The package block operation blocks usage rather than installing or uninstalling a plugin.
claims.quote: Block a Copilot package to prevent its usage. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/admin/catalog/packages/{id}/block

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specifically confirmed that Business apps (preview) appears in the Package Management API.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business apps" "copilotPackage"; "Business apps" "Cowork" "Work IQ MCP" block package management API. Opened Package Management overview/block and Cowork plugin setup. General plugin inventory is described, but this plugin's inclusion is not confirmed.

claims.claim: The whole Work IQ MCP server can be blocked through Microsoft 365 admin center > Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Block.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft 365 admin center. ... Select Agents > Tools. ... Select Work IQ MCP. ... To block access to the server, select Block.

claims.claim: The Work IQ MCP availability control applies to the whole server separately from Copilot audience settings and App Access.
claims.quote: This control applies to the entire Work IQ MCP server, separate from Copilot audience settings or App Access.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether blocking the whole Work IQ MCP server also stops this Cowork plugin.
claims.quote: Searched: "Business apps" "Cowork" "Work IQ MCP" block package management API. Opened manage-ai-experience-access, Cowork plugin setup, Business Applications overview and Manage plugins; none states how blocking Work IQ MCP affects this plugin.

claims.claim: Plugin installation, tenant audience, environment participation and App Access are separate controls.
claims.quote: These controls let administrators manage availability through Microsoft 365 Copilot, allow or block access to the Work IQ MCP server, and use App Access to control which applications can access data in an environment.

claims.claim: The feature's licensing model is consumption through Cowork rather than a separately named feature SKU.
claims.quote: Usage-based billing (UBB) charges for consumption rather than simply enabling a feature. ... Copilot Cowork: Work IQ consumption that supports a Cowork task is attributed to Cowork.

claims.claim: A variable cost rating is appropriate because consumption is metered in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Copilot credits are the unit used for the participating usage-based experiences. ... Complexity, the context needed, and the work performed affect consumption.
